production.malt: Single malt production uses 100% locally grown Cotswolds barley, floor-malted at Warminster Maltings before being milled at the distillery.
production.fermentation: Each mash yields about 2,500 litres of wort into stainless-steel washbacks. Two dried yeast strains, Anchor and Fermentis, are used and fermentation runs for more than 90 hours to encourage ester formation and fruity complexity.
production.stills: Whisky is double-distilled in copper pot stills. The distillery uses early cut points to capture fruity esters and switches to feints sooner than many distilleries to exclude heavier compounds; new make comes off the still at about 75% ABV.
production.maturation: New make is reduced to 63.5% ABV with demineralised water before filling into a range of oak casks for maturation.

houseCharacter: Cotswolds deliberately loads flavour into the wash through local floor-malted barley, two selected yeast strains and fermentation beyond 90 hours. Early spirit cuts then favour bright esters and limit heavier late-run compounds, producing a notably fruity new make before wood influence begins. The result is a distillate architecture aimed at orchard and tropical fruit intensity rather than relying on maturation alone to create flavour.
cask23Narrative: Cotswolds Distillery is unusually transparent about how it builds fruit into its whisky before the spirit ever reaches a cask. More than 90 hours of fermentation, two selected yeast strains and an early spirit cut create a highly ester-driven new make, while locally grown barley anchors the whisky to its English origin. For customers, it is an excellent example of a modern distillery using fermentation and cut-point control as major flavour tools rather than treating cask maturation as the whole story.
